literature_hits.summary: YES — The abstract explicitly states that MEN2A is caused by a germline variant in the RET proto-oncogene, directly asserting a causal relationship between the two.

YES — The abstract explicitly states that Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) is caused by germline variants in the RET proto-oncogene, directly asserting a causal genetic relationship between RET and MEN 2A.

YES — The abstract explicitly asserts that oncogenic germline RET mutations are the cause of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN2), including MEN2A, establishing a direct causal relationship between RET and the syndrome.

YES — The abstract explicitly asserts a direct causal and clinical relationship between mutations in the RET proto-oncogene and multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN2), stating that RET mutations result in variable onset and severity of MEN2 and that understanding RET has improved detection and management of MEN2 patients.

YES — The abstract explicitly states that RET was identified as the "primary driver" of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN2) syndrome, directly asserting a causal relationship between RET and MEN2A (a subtype of MEN2).

YES — The abstract explicitly asserts that germline mutations in the RET gene underlie Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A, directly linking RET as the causative genetic factor for the MEN-2 associated phenotypes.

YES – The abstract explicitly asserts that activating point mutations of the RET proto-oncogene are causally linked to MEN2A (and other hereditary MTC syndromes) by stating they occur in virtually all inherited cases, including MEN2A.

interaction_note: BioGRID edges are physical/genetic interactions, NOT activating/inhibiting mechanisms.
druggability_note: druggability_context is informational reader context only. It does not affect tractability_score, unmet_need_score, composite_score, STRONG_MATCH, or any pipeline filter.
pathway_neighbor_note: Pathway-neighbor expansion is lazy: the Chemist triggers it only when the primary target's own approved-drug pool is thin (< PATHWAY_NEIGHBOR_MIN_APPROVED candidates).  Discovered neighbors are tagged target_discovery_method='pathway_neighbor'.
